previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Addison’s disease presented with symptoms of early adrenal crisis, including muscle cramps, fatigue, body aches, and headache, after becoming dehydrated in the heat two days prior. She had attempted self-management with increased fluids and salt intake. In the emergency department, no electrolyte abnormalities or hypotension were found. She was admitted for observation and treatment, receiving IV fluids and a temporary increase in prednisone to 10 mg in the morning and 5 mg at night. Her symptoms resolved during the hospital stay, and she was discharged home on prednisone 10 mg daily with instructions to contact her endocrinologist to plan a taper back to her baseline dose. All other medications were continued as usual.
problems: Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
